# fshy: Email in full

> Sending, receiving, forwarding and inbox APIs.

Data as of 2026-11-10, the date of the published data. Version `e7cf1b4a40af`: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of every record's Markdown, topic by topic in the one order (hosted before self-hosted, then verdict, provider name, record id); it changes whenever a record does.

How to read a record, and the other topics: https://fshy.ajam.dev/llms-full.txt. One line per record: https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/email.md.

## Amazon SES

- `email/amazon-ses` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category transactional sender and relay
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-22T03:20:00.000Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-22
- url https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/amazon.md
- free tier: 3,000 message charges/month for the first 12 months, or $200 of AWS credits over 6 months for new accounts | unit: requests | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: not applicable
- retention: not applicable | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: an outbound sender | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: card | detail: an AWS account with a payment method
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate: 3,000 message charges per month for 12 months from first use [1]
  - write-gated (binding): the account starts in the sandbox and sends only to verified identities until a quota-increase request is approved [1]
- binding note: the sandbox blocks arbitrary recipients from the first send; the 3,000/month is second.
- interface detail: https://email.REGION.amazonaws.com, and the SES SMTP endpoint
- tooling: aws-cli, any SMTP client
- composes with: the cheapest real bulk rate in the topic, USD 0.10 per 1,000, behind a sandbox that every new account starts in. It composes with Plunk self-host as the paid chain.
- reliability: the sandbox is a write gate on every new account and the quota increase is a support request
- extras:
  - stale_after_days: 90
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: 'Receive up to 3,000 message charges for free each month for the first 12 months after you start using SES', and the sandbox restriction
  - [1] 2026-10-22: 'Starting July 15, 2025, new AWS customers will receive up to $200 in AWS Free Tier credits' with a 6-month free plan
- sources:
  - [1] https://aws.amazon.com/ses/faqs/
  - [2] https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/

## Brevo

- `email/brevo` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category transactional sender
- needs card no, phone unknown, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-30T09:26:49.193Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-30
- url https://www.brevo.com/pricing/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/brevo.md
- free tier: 300 email sends per day with no time limit; 100,000 contacts stored | unit: requests | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1] | note: Every email sent from the Free plan carries the Sent with Brevo sticker; up to 2,000 unique contacts can enter active automations; one user. Once the 300 daily sends are used, no campaign can be scheduled for the next day. The Free plan's limits page names no restriction on recipients.
- per-object cap: not applicable: a send count rather than an object
- retention: unused sends do not roll over | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: an outbound sender | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: Signup asks for an email and a password, or a Google or Apple sign-in, with no card; the account then verifies the email and asks for basic business information. Whether a mobile phone number with an SMS code is also required is unverified: behind a sign-up; users on the vendor's community forum report a phone number and SMS code step during registration. A sender on a free domain such as gmail.com cannot be authenticated, and the vendor states that mail from a free address is rejected or filtered to spam, so delivery needs a domain the sender controls.
- interface: rest, cli
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 300 sends per day, resetting daily, with no carry-over [2]
  - request-rate (binding): a campaign to more than 300 recipients delivers to 300 that day and needs a manual requeue, so the daily send counter is the campaign's limit too [2]
  - write-gated: transactional sending over SMTP or the API needs a separate activation by the vendor, requested by a support ticket from the account, before the first send; the time it takes is unverified: behind a sign-up [3]
- limits note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 100,000 contacts stored on the free plan. The campaign entry is a rate: the same 300-a-day counter is what a campaign meets, so it stays request-rate
- binding note: 300/day. The campaign path is the trap: a 1,000-contact list takes four days.
- interface detail: the SMTP relay and the transactional API; SMTP is the documented path
- tooling: any SMTP client, or the Brevo API
- composes with: the highest card-free daily cap found: 300/day, which is three times Resend's. It is the outbound half of the inbound-plus-outbound chain and its scarce link is the day.
- reliability: once the daily limit is hit, up to 1,000 transactional emails are held in a retry queue and anything beyond that is not delivered
- notes: The help page states the campaign behaviour explicitly, which is why the 300/day figure is not the whole answer for a marketing send.
- evidence note: no message was sent, so no delivery is proved. The submission path was probed: smtp-relay.brevo.com:587 answered 250, STARTTLS completed against the system trust store, and AUTH LOGIN returned 334
- extras:
  - stale_after_days: 90
- evidence:
  - [2] 2026-10-22: 'The Free plan includes 300 email sends per day', unused sends do not roll over, and a campaign above 300 recipients needs the Requeue option on successive days
  - [4] 2026-10-22: 'Send 300 emails a day with the best free SMTP server'
  - probe:smtp://smtp-relay.brevo.com:587 2026-10-22: banner 250, EHLO advertises SIZE and 8BITMIME, STARTTLS completed against the system trust store, and AUTH LOGIN returned 334. The submission endpoint answers; no message was sent

If you've never sent transactional emails from your account, contact our support team by creating a ticket from your account to request activation.

Emails beyond this queue are not delivered.

## Buttondown

- `email/buttondown` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category newsletter sender with a REST API | tier free
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-02T10:00:26.325Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-03
- url https://buttondown.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/buttondown.md
- free tier: free for the first 100 subscribers, with the price assuming at most one email a day to the whole subscriber base; API included, no card | unit: users | metered on: identity-count | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1] | note: The quota counts subscribers, not messages. Sending from a custom domain is free; without one, mail goes out from the account's username at buttondown.email. Attachments, tagging and segmentation, automations and archives on a custom domain are paid add-ons. Subscribers are confirmed by double opt-in unless created through the API with type regular.
- per-object cap: not applicable: email attachments are a paid add-on
- retention: not stated
- egress: not applicable: an outbound sender | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: The register page asks for a username, an email address and a password, or Apple or Google sign-in, and states that no card is needed. Every new account is reviewed before it can send, and a verification form asks what the newsletter is about, who its audience is, where imported subscribers came from, and details of the person or organization. No domain is needed: mail goes out from the username at buttondown.email by default. A custom sending domain is free, set up either by delegating a subdomain with two NS records (managed) or by adding the records shown in settings (manual).
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): the free price assumes at most one email a day to the whole subscriber base; more needs a contact with the vendor [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 600 API requests per minute on every endpoint, and 100 subscriber creations per day through POST /v1/subscribers [2]
  - write-gated: every new account is reviewed before it can send, most reviews within one to three business days [3]
  - request-rate (binding): new senders are capped per hour until they reach a baseline of engagement and reputation; the figure is not stated [4]
- limits note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 100 subscribers on the free plan.
- binding note: one email a day to at most 100 subscribers: the subscriber ceiling caps the recipients and the daily assumption caps the sends.
- interface detail: the REST API at https://api.buttondown.com/v1 with an OpenAPI spec: POST /v1/emails creates an email for the subscriber base; POST /v1/subscribers/{id_or_email}/emails/{email_id} takes no request body and sends an existing finalized email to one subscriber, and a draft is refused with a 400 whose code is email_invalid_status; POST /v1/emails/{id}/send-draft delivers a draft to the subscriber ids and email addresses named in its body, the documented route for sending drafts for review
- tooling: curl or any HTTP client; there is no official SDK, and typed clients are generated from the OpenAPI spec
- composes with: a list sender rather than a transactional relay: every recipient is a subscriber, so it carries a newsletter or a notification list of up to 100 people, and per-message transactional mail belongs on a relay.
- reliability: sending is disabled temporarily when unsubscribes, complaints or hard bounces run high on a new sender
- notes: The vendor's summary file (llms.txt) lists API access and custom domains under a USD 9 Basic plan, while the API page, the plan badge on the API guides and the January 2025 pricing post place API access on the free plan, and the sending-domain page and the pricing page place custom-domain sending there; the summary file is out of date.
- evidence note: no message was sent and no authenticated request was made; the free plan, the API on the free plan, the finalized-only rule of the per-subscriber send endpoint and the rate limits are documented, while the response a free account's key gets from that endpoint, whether an email can reach a final status without a send to the list, and the account review with its verification form are unverified: behind a sign-up.
- extras:
  - stale_after_days: 90

- per-object cap: 25 MiB inbound message; larger messages are rejected | bytes: 26214400 | source: [2]
- retention: not applicable: messages are forwarded, not stored | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: inbound only on the free plan | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: a Cloudflare account with the domain delegated to Cloudflare nameservers
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: 25 MiB inbound message; larger messages are rejected [2]
- limits note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 200 destination addresses per account, shared across every domain; 200 routing rules per domain and 30 domains per zone
- binding note: nothing in the vocabulary binds the volume: inbound is unlimited and the 25 MiB message cap bounds a single message rather than a day. What actually caps the shape is the 200 destination addresses per account, which is a count and not one of the six kinds
- interface detail: MX records on the zone, with rules mapping a pattern to a destination or a Worker
- tooling: the Cloudflare dashboard, wrangler for Worker handlers
- composes with: the inbound half of the free mail chain and the only unmetered thing in this topic: unlimited inbound on a domain already held, forwarded to a mailbox. Its scarce link is the 200 verified destinations at the account level.
- reliability: a routing rule maps one pattern to one destination; a fan-out to several destinations needs a Worker
- notes: Inbound is genuinely unmetered and is the one unlimited thing in this topic. The 200-destination cap is the quiet one.
- evidence note: no probe: the inbound path could not be exercised from this host. route1, route2 and route3.mx.cloudflare.net answered 550 on the sender's IPv6 reverse lookup, and TCP 25 was reset over IPv4, so no SMTP-level evidence was obtained either way
- extras:
  - stale_after_days: 90
- evidence:

  - [2] 2026-10-22: 200 routing rules per domain, 200 destination addresses per account, and a 25 MiB inbound message limit

- composes with: an outbound sender at 100 a day that pairs with an inbound router such as Cloudflare Email Routing for the receiving half; the daily count is the scarce link.
- reliability: an account placed Under Review has delivery paused; mail submitted meanwhile is queued and sent if the account is reactivated
- notes: The 3,000 a month is the 100 a day summed over 30 days, so the monthly figure cannot be spent in a burst.
- evidence note: no message was sent, so no delivery is proved; smtp.elasticemail.com answered a 220 banner on ports 587 and 2525. The account verification step and any phone check are behind a sign-up.

- tooling: wrangler, the Cloudflare API

- free tier: no free plan: a free trial of up to 30 days with no card, capped at 120 sent messages per day; the cheapest plan with custom domains and IMAP is Individual at $5 per month, billed as $60 for 12 months | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-31 | source: [1] | note: Individual is $6 month to month, $114 for 24 months or $168 for 36 months. Duo is $96 for 12 months for two users and Family $132 for 12 months for up to six. Basic ($36 for 12 months, 6 GB) allows no custom domains and includes no IMAP or SMTP.
- per-object cap: 70 MB per message sent or received, which usually means an attachment of no more than 50 MB | source: [2]
- retention: 50 GB for mail, calendar and contacts plus 10 GB of file storage on Individual; mail over quota is soft-bounced, then hard-bounced after a week; an unpaid trial loses sending and receiving, then is disabled and deleted | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: a mailbox; sending is capped at 8,000 messages and 2 GB per day per user on Individual, and at 120 messages per day on a trial | metered: yes | free allowance: 120 sent messages per day on a trial account | source: [2]
- identity: card | detail: the trial asks for a name, a new address on a Fastmail domain or an own domain, and a password, with no card, and may ask for a mobile phone number for an SMS code; a trial user not verified by SMS cannot read mail over IMAP or POP. The paid plan accepts credit and debit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay, and no cash or bank transfer.
- interface: unknown, webdav
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 8,000 messages and 2 GB sent per day per user on Individual; the hourly limit is half the daily and the 10-minute limit half the hourly [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 120 messages sent per day on a trial account [3]
  - volume-quota: 50 GB of mail storage and 10 GB of file storage per user on Individual [2]
  - per-object-cap: 70 MB per message [2]
  - write-gated: a trial user not verified by SMS cannot download mail over IMAP or POP [3]
- binding note: on a trial the 120 messages per day bind first; on Individual the 8,000 per day is the first stated ceiling, and storage of 50 GB rarely binds before it.
- interface detail: IMAP at imap.fastmail.com (993), POP at pop.fastmail.com and SMTP at smtp.fastmail.com (465, or 587 with STARTTLS), all with an app password and TLS only; WebDAV file access at https://webdav.fastmail.com/; CalDAV and CardDAV. Basic plans include no IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV or CardDAV
- endpoint: https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
- tooling: any IMAP, POP or SMTP client with an app password; JMAP over HTTP and JSON with an API token; any WebDAV client for files
- composes with: a full mailbox with custom domains, IMAP, WebDAV files and 8,000 sends per day at $60 a year; the price buys 50 GB and send volume rather than a low entry cost.
- reliability: accounts found sending duplicative email are closed permanently; an unpaid trial loses sending and receiving, then is disabled and deleted
- notes: No free custom-domain mailbox. The cheapest plan with custom domains is Individual at $60 for 12 months; Basic is cheaper at $36 for 12 months but has neither custom domains nor IMAP and SMTP.
- evidence note: prices and limits read from the vendor pages; imap.fastmail.com:993 accepted a TCP connection and smtp.fastmail.com:587 answered with an ESMTP banner; no login or send was made

The 4-month Discovery offer, chosen at signup or later in the account, is a single payment of EUR 6 that gives the Premium plan for 4 months and keeps the address for life; it is paid, not free. The features table lists customized domain names under Premium. Family is EUR 3 per month for up to 5 Premium accounts in a Family space, and Pro Start EUR 3.60 per month with tax for 2 accounts sharing 50 GB. Declaring an external domain is free; a domain bought at Mailo starts at EUR 15 per year with tax.
- per-object cap: 50 MB of attachments per message on Premium, 25 MB on Free; larger files are sent as download links, up to 1 GB on Premium and 500 MB on Free | source: [2]
- retention: a 20 GB mailbox on Premium; a full mailbox refuses new mail; a Premium account is never deleted for inactivity, a Free account after 365 days without access | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: a mailbox; unverified: no hourly or daily sending cap is published on the captured pages | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: card | detail: signup asks for a last name, a first name and a date of birth, all compulsory, a gender, a security question or rescue email address, and a computed proof-of-work check, with no phone field; accounts are for ages 13 and above. - interface detail: IMAP at mail.mailo.com (993, SSL/TLS; 143 answers with an IMAP4rev1 banner offering STARTTLS) and SMTP at mail.mailo.com (465, SSL/TLS; 587 also answers); POP3 on subscribed accounts only; ActiveSync; CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV
- tooling: any IMAP or SMTP client, with the full address as username; application passwords are supported
- composes with: a domain registered elsewhere is declared in a Mailo space free of charge, with its DNS records changed at the registrar, or a domain is bought at Mailo from EUR 15 per year with tax; a single mailbox on that domain then takes the Premium offer.
- reliability: a full mailbox refuses new mail and the sender receives a non-delivery notice
- notes: No free custom-domain mailbox: Mailo Free has IMAP but no custom domain. Premium is €1.50 per month for one mailbox; per mailbox, Family at €3 per month for up to 5 Premium accounts costs less.

Mini is $9/month or $90/year with 1000 in/day, 100 out/day and 30 GB. Limits are counted per account across all its domains and mailboxes.
- per-object cap: unverified: no maximum message or attachment size is stated on the captured pages
- retention: no hard storage quota: the 5 GB of Micro is soft and mail never bounces for full storage; an account over quota for seven days is blocked and, uncleared, purged after 30 days | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: a mailbox; outbound mail is counted in messages, 20 per day on Micro with a 25% tolerance before sends are rejected | metered: yes | free allowance: 20 outgoing messages per day on Micro | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: signup asks for a full name and an existing email address that receives a confirmation link, with an optional organization name; no card for the trial. The paid plan is paid by card through Stripe, by a PayPal prepayment to the account balance, or in Bitcoin arranged through support. Domains on free TLDs are refused, so a paid domain is needed.
- interface: unknown, rest
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 20 outgoing messages per day on Micro, per account, with up to 25% tolerance before sends are rejected [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 200 incoming messages per day on Micro, per account; past the 25% tolerance incoming mail is deferred to the next day [1]
  - volume-quota: 5 GB of soft storage on Micro, per account [1]
- binding note: 20 outgoing messages per day is the first ceiling on Micro; storage is soft and mailboxes and addresses are unlimited.
- interface detail: IMAP at imap.migadu.com (993, TLS), POP at pop.migadu.com (995, TLS) and SMTP at smtp.migadu.com (465, TLS; port 587 also answers); CalDAV and CardDAV; an administration REST API in early beta at https://api.migadu.com/v1/ with HTTP Basic authentication by account email and API key
- endpoint: part of interface detail
- tooling: any IMAP, POP or SMTP client; IMAPSync for migration per the vendor guides; the beta REST API manages domains and mailboxes
- composes with: a flat-priced account with unlimited mailboxes and addresses across many domains; 20 outgoing messages per day bind first on Micro, so it suits receiving on many domains more than sending.
- reliability: a trial account can be limited or ended without notice; an account over quota for seven days is blocked and purged 30 days later
- notes: No free custom-domain mailbox: the cheapest plan is Micro at $19/year, with unlimited mailboxes but 20 outgoing messages per day. The trial needs only an email address. Pricing is per account, not per mailbox.
- evidence note: plans and quotas read from the vendor pages; imap.migadu.com:993 accepted a TCP connection and smtp.migadu.com:587 answered with an ESMTP banner; no login or send was made

- identity: card | detail: the paid signup charges $10 through Stripe; the free trial needs an SMS-capable phone to activate. Signup asks for an administrator username on a shared domain and a password, with a recovery email or phone recommended.
- interface: unknown, webdav
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): approximately 3000 external messages per day, or 300 at once, per account [3]
  - request-rate (binding): very low external sending limits on trial accounts [3]
- binding note: Simple pricing sets no hard limit on users, domains or storage, so the external sending rate is the first stated ceiling.
- interface detail: IMAP at imap.purelymail.com (993, SSL/TLS), SMTP at smtp.purelymail.com (465 SSL/TLS, or 587 with STARTTLS), POP3 at pop3.purelymail.com (995), ManageSieve at mailserver.purelymail.com (4190); WebDAV, CardDAV and CalDAV for basic file storage, contacts and calendars
- tooling: any IMAP, POP3 or SMTP client; IMAP IDLE; Sieve filters over ManageSieve or in webmail
- composes with: a flat $10 a year for unlimited mailboxes on unlimited owned domains, with external sending capped near 3000 messages per day; a fit for many addresses on domains already owned.
- reliability: an account broken into and used to send spam is locked
- notes: No free custom-domain mailbox; Simple pricing at $10 a year covers unlimited users on unlimited owned domains, with external sending near 3000 messages per day as the first stated ceiling.
- evidence note: prices and limits read from the vendor pages; imap.purelymail.com:993 accepted a TCP connection and smtp.purelymail.com:587 answered with an SMTP banner; no login or send was made

## Tuta (formerly Tutanota)

- `email/tuta` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category end-to-end encrypted mailbox | tier Revolutionary
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T05:33:22.975Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://tuta.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/tuta.md
- free tier: no free custom-domain mailbox: the Free plan has 1 GB of storage and no custom domains; Revolutionary at €3 per month paid yearly adds 20 GB, 15 extra addresses and 3 custom domains | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-31 | source: [1] | note: Legend is EUR 8 per month paid yearly with 500 GB, 30 extra addresses and 10 custom domains. Prices include taxes. Free accounts are deleted after more than six months without a login. No sending cap number is published: the support page says email limits are calculated for each account from several variables, and limits for paying users are much higher.
- per-object cap: 25 MB attachments on every plan | source: [1]
- retention: 20 GB on Revolutionary; a Free account is deleted after more than six months without a login | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable: a mailbox with no IMAP, POP or SMTP access from Tuta; mail is read and sent through the Tuta web, desktop and mobile apps, or through an unofficial bridge to Tuta's native API | metered: no | source: [3]
- identity: anonymous | detail: signup asks the user to choose a new Tuta address and a password, and the vendor's sign-up guide states that it asks for no verification of any kind, no phone number among them; an account may be held for approval for up to 48 hours, which choosing a paid plan skips. Custom domains need a paid plan, paid by credit card, PayPal, or a gift card bought with Monero, Bitcoin or cash through a partner.
- interface: unknown
- limits:
  - retention-clamped: no IMAP, POP or SMTP access from Tuta: its own apps are the supported clients, and unofficial bridges reach the mail through Tuta's native API [3]
  - write-gated (binding): custom domains need a paid plan: 3 on Revolutionary, 10 on Legend, none on Free [1]
  - volume-quota: 20 GB of storage on Revolutionary, 1 GB on Free [1]
  - per-object-cap: 25 MB attachments [1]
  - request-rate: unverified: no sending cap number is published; email limits are calculated for each account from several variables, an account over its limit is stopped for a day or two, and limits for paying users are much higher [4]
- limits note: no vocabulary kind names a removed mail protocol; it is filed as retention-clamped, as in the Zoho Mail record, and the true kind is a protocol gate
- binding note: a custom domain needs a paid plan: the Free plan has none, Revolutionary at €3 per month paid yearly has 3 and Legend at €8 per month paid yearly has 10, so a custom-domain mailbox starts at the Revolutionary price.
- interface detail: Tuta's own web, desktop and mobile apps; Tuta offers no IMAP, POP or SMTP, which it states it cannot offer with end-to-end encryption
- tooling: Tuta's own web, desktop and mobile apps, open source under GPLv3 with Tuta's Rust SDK in the same repository; Tuta offers no IMAP, POP or SMTP. Unofficial open-source bridges serve IMAP and SMTP over Tuta's API: TutaBridge (Rust; a desktop app or a CLI binary) and tuta-proxy (Python or Docker; also CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV); the user installs and runs the bridge beside the mail client or script that uses it.
- composes with: an end-to-end encrypted mailbox for up to 3 custom domains at €3 per month paid yearly (Revolutionary), or 10 at €8 per month (Legend), read and sent through Tuta's own web, desktop and mobile apps, or by a script or mail client through an unofficial IMAP and SMTP bridge to Tuta's API that the user installs and runs.
- reliability: a Free account is deleted after more than six months without a login; a new signup may be held for approval for up to 48 hours
- notes: A custom-domain mailbox at €3 per month paid yearly on Revolutionary, with 3 custom domains, 20 GB and 15 extra addresses; the Free plan carries no custom domain, so the verdict is paid-only. Tooling records the missing IMAP, POP and SMTP and the bridges that add IMAP and SMTP.
- evidence note: plans and prices read from the rendered pricing page; protocol support read from vendor blog posts; no account was made

- retention: not stated | source: [1]
- egress: not applicable | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: any-phone | detail: a Yandex ID: name and surname, a username, a password, and a mobile phone number confirmed by an SMS code; the registration help names no country

- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): a custom domain requires a Yandex 360 for Business plan, from USD 3.99 per employee per month on Basic as 360.yandex.com lists it [1]
- limits note: reported by third-party posts that quote a notice sent to organizations without a plan, and stated on no first-party page read: IMAP, SMTP and POP3 become unavailable without a Yandex 360 plan from the date in the notice, June 29 in the first notice quoted and later dates in later notices, leaving webmail and the mobile app; the same posts report that personal mailboxes are not affected, and whether non-profit organizations that keep the services free are affected is unverified
- interface detail: webmail and the mobile apps, and IMAP at imap.yandex.com (port 993, SSL) and SMTP at smtp.yandex.com (port 465, SSL; port 587 for a connection opened without encryption) with an app password, for personal mailboxes and for organization mailboxes where an administrator enables the protocols; the custom-domain feature is a business-plan SKU
- tooling: web mail and the official mobile app; an organization admin can enable IMAP for email clients under Mail settings
- composes with: a mailbox rather than a sender, and the custom-domain feature that would make it useful moved behind the paid tier.
- reliability: an organization that used the free version moves to a paid plan in stages: it keeps the features free until it receives an email 7 days before its first payment, and if it does not pay it stays in view-only mode, where its data is kept and readable and nothing new can be added
- notes: Non-profit organizations and charities keep all Yandex 360 for Business services free of charge, so mail on a custom domain stays free on that institutional route.

## MailerSend

- `email/mailersend` | fails-quota | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category transactional sender
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T05:33:30.050Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://www.mailersend.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/mailersend.md
- free tier: 500 emails/month on the Free plan once the account is approved, with a daily quota of 100 API and SMTP relay requests; 1 domain, 1 API token, 1 webhook, 1 template | unit: requests | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-10-31 | source: [1] | note: Sandbox mode, open with no payment method, gives 100 emails a month with a cap of 100 API requests a day, to any 2 recipients until the account is approved, with no time limit
- per-object cap: not applicable
- retention: 1-day activity data retention on the free plan | days: 1 | source: [1]
- egress: not applicable: an outbound sender | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: signup needs an email address, confirmed from a verification email sent to that address; approval then asks for details of the company or organization and how the service will be used, and takes up to 48 hours; Sandbox mode needs no payment method; the Free plan is subscribed on the Plan and billing page with an organization address and credit card information, after the account is approved, and is not charged
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 500 emails per month [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 100 API or SMTP relay requests per day on the Free plan; every request counts against the quota, which resets at midnight UTC [2]
- limits note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 1 sending domain, 1 API token, 1 webhook, 1 template. The daily 100 is a quota of API and SMTP relay requests on the rate-limit, SMTP relay and developer pages and in the plans table (Daily API requests), and the plans help page prose calls it a daily limit of 100 emails; how many emails one request may carry on the Free plan is not stated
- interface detail: the MailerSend email API and SMTP relay
- tooling: curl, any SMTP client
- composes with: composes with a domain and with nothing that needs volume.
- reliability: sending pauses when the monthly limit is reached and resumes when the 30-day period resets; the Free plan allows no extra usage
- notes: The 14-day Professional trial at the top of the pricing page needs a payment method and ends on the Free plan; Sandbox mode needs no payment method.
